# Temple Scroll Column 28 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 28 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 28:3 — "porches" vs. "porticoes" vs. "covered entrance halls"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "porches" | Simple English for the gate structures |
| LOGOS | "porticoes" | Classical architectural term |
| PNEUMA | "covered entrance halls" | Descriptive modern phrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET: "porches." Consistent with the rendering of ulam established in Column 26. "Porticoes" imports Greco-Roman associations; PNEUMA's phrase is verbose.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 28:8 — "chambers" vs. "upper rooms"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "chambers" | Standard term for temple rooms |
| LOGOS | "chambers" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "upper rooms" | Specifies the elevated position above the gates |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS: "chambers." The text already specifies "above the gates," making "upper" redundant. "Chambers" is the established temple vocabulary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 28:9 — "chief of the priests" vs. "chief priest" vs. "chief priest" / "chief of the army" vs. "commander" vs. "military commander"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "chief of the priests... chief of the army of Israel" | Literal construct chains |
| LOGOS | "chief priest... commander of the army of Israel" | Standard English titles |
| PNEUMA | "chief priest... military commander" | Concise modern titles |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "chief priest... commander of the army of Israel." "Commander" is appropriate for sar tseva; retaining "of Israel" preserves the national scope. PNEUMA's "military commander" is redundant.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 28:11 — "divisions" vs. "priestly divisions" vs. "priestly rotations"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "divisions" | Simple rendering of mishmarot |
| LOGOS | "priestly divisions" | Specifies the priestly context |
| PNEUMA | "priestly rotations" | Modern term for the shift-based system |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET: "divisions." The priestly context is clear from "overseers"; "rotations" is overly modern.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 28:15 — "first of their dough" vs. "first portion of their dough" vs. "first of their bread dough"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "first of their dough" | Literal rendering of reshit arisoteikhem |
| LOGOS | "first portion of their dough" | Adds "portion" for clarity |
| PNEUMA | "first of their bread dough" | Adds "bread" to specify the type |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET: "first of their dough." The Hebrew is concise; LOGOS and PNEUMA add unnecessary words. The meaning is clear in context.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 28:16 — "sons of Israel" vs. "children of Israel" vs. "people of Israel"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sons of Israel" | Literal rendering of benei Yisrael |
| LOGOS | "children of Israel" | Traditional inclusive rendering |
| PNEUMA | "people of Israel" | Modern inclusive rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "children of Israel." Traditional rendering that is both inclusive and established in English Bible tradition. "People" (PNEUMA) loses the familial/genealogical connotation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
